title: Family buyer worried 900 sqft is too small
buyer_primary_need: Determine whether the 900 sq.ft. Type A layout can practically accommodate a family of four, especially bedroom, furniture, and living/dining circulation needs.
key_information_learned: The buyer is a family of four: buyer, spouse, and two children.
The family uses a 4-seater dining table.
Their current home feels more open; they are concerned about sofa/table fit and circulation.
The buyer is open to viewing the show unit specifically to assess living/dining flow and asks for available days and times.
important_information_missed: The buyer's sofa size was not established, but the buyer stopped responding to that question and the conversation progressed appropriately to a viewing.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: 900 sqft for a family sounds quite small leh.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Fair concern—900 sqft isn’t a large unit. It’s a 3-bedroom, 2-bathroom layout, and the project materials describe all three bedrooms as able to fit a queen bed, with relatively little space taken up by corridors. Whether it feels comfortable really depends on your family’s needs. How many people would be staying there?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Four of us—me, my spouse and two kids. Queen beds fitting is good to know, but I’m also wondering whether there’s enough space to move around and fit our dining table and sofa without everything feeling squeezed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: That’s a fair thing to check for a family of four. The living, dining and kitchen area is about 404.7 sq ft combined—not living space alone. The layout is described as having little wasted corridor, but whether your sofa and dining table leave enough room to move depends on their size. Do you usually use a 4- or 6-seater dining table?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Usually a 4-seater. Our current place feels more open, so I’m trying to picture whether the sofa and table would leave enough room to move around in this layout.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: That makes sense—if your current place feels more open, it’s worth checking the furniture fit rather than assuming it’ll feel the same. With a 4-seater, the sofa’s size and placement will make a big difference to the walking space. Roughly how long is your sofa?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: The layout is much easier to judge in person than from the floor area alone. You could see how the living and dining space feels for your family—would you be open to viewing the show unit?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Yeah, I’d be open to seeing the show unit—mainly to check the living/dining flow. What days and times are available?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Great—seeing the show unit should help you judge the living and dining flow. Let me get the viewing arrangements checked, and the team will follow up with the available days and times.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: The viewing calendar isn’t connected here, so I can’t verify available days or times or confirm a booking.

commercial_progression_evidence: Turn 1 acknowledged that 900 sq.ft. is not large, used sourced layout information, and asked a relevant household-size question.
Turns 2–3 connected the buyer's furniture and circulation concern to the actual layout rather than claiming it would feel spacious.
Turn 4 proposed viewing the show unit as a practical way to judge the unresolved flow concern.
After the buyer accepted and asked about viewing times, turn 5 handed off for operational slot checking.
judge.strongest_ai_move: It acknowledged the size trade-off, tied the response to the family's specific furniture/circulation concern, and proposed an in-person layout check without promising the unit would feel roomy.
judge.weakest_ai_move: After the buyer described the sofa/table circulation concern and supplied the 4-seater detail, the Agent asked for sofa length rather than immediately offering the relevant show-unit check. This was a minor delay; it progressed to a viewing invitation on the next turn.
missed_selling_opportunity: Could have invited the buyer to assess the family layout slightly earlier, after learning that circulation and furniture fit were the central concern.
remaining_knowledge_gaps: Viewing availability could not be verified because the calendar was not connected in this run.
judge.summary: The AI successfully progressed a suitable, convertible buyer to appointment-ready status and made a correctly timed operational appointment handoff. The buyer explicitly accepted a show-unit viewing and asked for available times; this is viewing interest, not an accepted specific appointment, so no booking is confirmed. The Human executor could not verify slots, and the requested operational task was not completed. No support request was made or needed: the retrieved Knowledge addressed general layout claims, while the scenario's synthetic furniture overlay was not requested. The primary question is answered positively for this run: the AI used relevant information, continued selling, and moved the buyer toward Appointment Ready. This single no-support run does not test support-enabled resumption. No post-handoff AI message or session return occurred.
judge.improvement_recommendation: When a buyer has explained that furniture fit and circulation are the remaining concern, move to the show-unit invitation promptly rather than continuing another furniture-dimension question if the physical viewing is the practical way to resolve uncertainty. No repository source change is indicated.
judge.simulator_only_evidence: No support fixture was requested or used. The synthetic layout-overlay measurements in the scenario were not communicated to the buyer and are not Pearlmont Knowledge or evidence of live operational capability.
